subject: Urolithin A restores calcium-driven organelle crosstalk to trigger mitophagy and slow ageing
script: From Agewell Brief: Urolithin A restores calcium-driven organelle crosstalk to trigger mitophagy and slow ageing. A gut metabolite reopens ER–mitochondria–lysosome communication via calcium sparks, reviving mitochondrial quality control and extending healthspan in worms and human cells. UA releases ER calcium, driving DRP-1 fission and mitophagy. Calcium chelation blocks UA's benefits on muscle and lifespan. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
